subject: Proposal: Unlocking Min Commit with Split Invoicing & Tax Routing
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlanticai.com>, procurement@atlanticai.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Unlocking Min Commit with Split Invoicing & Tax Routing

Team / Maya —

Following our call last week, Atlantic AI is comfortable with the list price but needs flexibility on cashflow: they want to avoid a single large upfront invoice tied to the full annual minimum commit. Legal is pushing back on multi-entity invoicing and tax evidence, which is stalling signature.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Split the min commit into quarterly invoicing tranches tied to usage thresholds (not pro rata).
- Route invoice 1 to Atlantic AI UK (VAT-registered) with VAT handling; invoices 2–4 to Atlantic AI US entity — adds cashflow flexibility while preserving net economics.
- Redwood issues a single Order Form referencing the MSA; commercial appendix enumerates invoice recipients and tax IDs.
- Add a one-way credit note mechanism if an entity is unable to accept an invoice (fallback to consolidated invoice).

Asks:
1) Kim — can Legal accept an appendix-based entity routing clause (we keep commercial terms in the order form, not the MSA)?
2) Ben — can Payments/Ops accept split invoicing with two different billing recipients and produce mapping for AR? I attached a rough billing_mapping.xlsx.
3) Maya / Procurement — can you provide the VAT ID for the UK entity and confirm the US billing email for PO routing?

I attached a redline (redlined_orderform_v3.pdf) that maps the proposed appendix language to the current order form. This is intended as a narrow commercial compromise to get to signature while preserving revenue recognition profiles.

Thanks,
Rafael
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redlined_orderform_v3.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: billing_mapping.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlanticai.com>, procurement@atlanticai.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Unlocking Min Commit with Split Invoicing & Tax Routing

Rafael —

Thanks for outlining. High level, Legal is open to a commercial appendix in the Order Form if the MSA remains the single source of truth for liability and data terms. A couple of constraints and clarifying asks from Legal & Tax:

1) Tax evidence: we need entity-level tax certificates (VAT registration, W-9 for US entity) before we route VAT-bearing invoices. For UK VAT we need the registration number and effective date.
2) Invoicing recipient change: Legal prefers we avoid automatic fallback to a different entity that could trigger indemnity/collection challenges. If we do a fallback, it should be explicit, manual, and require a written confirmation from the customer point-of-contact.
3) Revenue recognition: Finance needs a clear mapping of tranche amounts and expected effective dates — Ben, can you confirm whether ops can emit four invoices that map to revenue in the quarter the invoice is issued?
4) Contract language: Suggested addition to appendix — a short table (entity name | billing recipient | tax id | currency | fallback instructions). That keeps the legal language minimal.

I redlined a couple of clauses in your PDF (comments inline). If Maya can share the VAT ID and the US tax docs, we can finalize today and push to SignNow.

-Kim
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear summary. We can do the split invoicing approach. Quick answers below:

- UK VAT ID: GB123456789 (Atlantic AI UK Ltd) — effective 2025-02-01.
- US tax doc: W-9 for Atlantic AI, EIN 12-3456789. I attached the W-9 to the procurement mailbox (procurement@atlanticai.com) and copied procurement here.

On fallback: we agree that any manual switch should be confirmed in writing. Procurement will provide a single-authorized contact for such confirmations.

Thanks Maya — that's perfect and much appreciated.

Ben / Kim: based on Maya's details, here's the playbook I propose to get to signature by EOD tomorrow:

1) Kim — finalize the appendix table with the four fields (entity | billing recipient | tax id | fallback contact) and slide into the redlined_orderform_v3.pdf as a clean copy + a tracked copy.
2) Ben — Payments/Ops to confirm invoice sequence and AR mapping (I need a one-pager that ops can hand to customer finance explaining the four-tranche schedule, recognition timing, and PO mapping).
3) I will send a short email to the Atlantic AI AP contact (cc'd) confirming the PO routing addresses and requesting PO issuance by tomorrow morning.

If legal/ops both sign off, I'll route to SignNow and mark the HubSpot deal DA-8741 as 'Contract Sent'.

I'll drop the final PDF in the Drive link above and update the HubSpot deal with the comms template for AP.
